narrative.overview:
The page is drawn as one family of tickets. The hero is drawn with vectors only: on the brand-teal panel, a dot-matrix map of the world's land (Natural Earth's open data) carries five flight routes between real airports, four airport codes in small departure-board tags and one airplane in flight, beside the headline at the left; a boarding-pass-shaped booking bar is laid across the panel, the three promises and the Trustpilot score follow as one quiet glass bar, and the airline logos run along the panel's foot like a departures board. The reviews open with the Trustpilot score and continue in three cards of one kind; the four "Be ready" cards are the client's own ticket stubs on the same dotted map. One idea, repeated with the same geometry, from the first viewport to the last section.

Every colour is a production colour. The palette is the production theme's presets and the values its section styles resolve to (teal ink, brand teal, deep teal, a soft teal surface, one burnt-orange action) and nothing is invented. Type is the production face, Figtree, at weight 800 for the hero and 700 for sections. The artwork (the four illustrations, the nine airline logos) is the client's own; the map is computed from public-domain data by a script and the icons are Phosphor's, so nothing is drawn by hand and there is no photograph.

Density is calm: large type, generous space, surfaces that change by meaning (brand teal for the welcome and the instrument, white for reading and operating, a pale teal ground for the Trustpilot summary and "Be ready"). Motion is one entrance, one slow marquee that can be paused, and answers to input.
keyCharacteristics: An inset, rounded brand-teal panel on white; its content shares one left edge with the header and every section.

The booking form is a boarding pass (desktop): a white main half and a tinted stub with the fare and the CTA, a dashed perforation and two notches through which the panel shows. Below 1180px it becomes a white card.
One picture, and it is information: routes between real airports, the client's own dotted-globe motif made precise. It is masked out across the text column, so text never sits on it.
Ticket vocabulary everywhere: dashed perforation, semicircle notches, a barcode bar, small-caps stub labels, departure-board codes.
Burnt orange appears only on actions and on error text (the production's own choice).
A sideways airline-logo marquee as the foot of the panel, with a visible pause control.

rules.name: The No New Colour Rule
rules.body: If a value is not in the production palette it does not ship. `tools/palette-audit.js` renders the page and lists every colour painted; the map is drawn in white, aqua and accent-bright only.

rules.name: The One Hot Colour Rule
rules.body: Burnt orange marks the action and the error; never a heading, badge or background wash. Errors are never red.

rules.name: The Boundary Rule
rules.body: A control's edge uses control-line (3:1 minimum); hairlines are decoration and never the only boundary of something a person operates.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Figtree only. Weight, size and colour create hierarchy, never a second typeface.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, labels and buttons are sentence case; capitals are reserved for airport codes, stub labels and the strip title.

dos: Do keep the booking form the brightest, most finished object in the first viewport, with its CTA above the fold.
Do use only production colours, under their production names, and re-run the palette audit after any change.
Do carry the ticket vocabulary (perforation, notch, stub label, departure-board code) into every new component.
Do keep the airline marquee pausable and give reduced-motion users a static row.
Do give every control a 44px minimum target and a control-line boundary, and every text link at least 24px.
Do rebuild the map with its script (open data, computed routes) instead of editing or redrawing it.
donts: Don't add a colour, a second typeface, a photograph or a stock illustration; the artwork is the client's, the map is computed from open data and the icons are Phosphor's.
Don't use red for errors, gradient text, or orange for anything but actions and errors.

Don't let the map reach the text: it is masked out across the text column and hidden below 900px, so the headline, lead and tabs keep 4.5:1 or better (3:1 for the large aqua word), measured on the rendered page.
Don't fade text or the form while they animate; entrance effects slide them without changing their contrast (only the map behind them fades in).
Don't animate on hover anything that is not a link or a button.
